proposed_title: AP Tracker Snapshot: 5 of 25 Trump Promises Kept, 9 In Progress and 11 Complicated
description_medium: The AP promise-tracker dataset, retrieved October 2, 2026, declares a last-modified date of December 3, 2025. Its 25 selected Trump campaign promises were labeled 5 “Kept,” 9 “In progress” and 11 “It’s complicated.” These counts describe AP’s tracker classifications at that dataset timestamp. They do not establish a broader score for all campaign commitments or verify the entry’s earlier claim that Trump was “behind.”
description_long: The Associated Press tracker follows a selected set of promises Donald Trump made during his 2024 campaign. The tracker data retrieved on October 2, 2026 declares that it was last modified December 3, 2025. In that dated dataset, AP listed 25 promises: five labeled “Kept,” nine labeled “In progress” and eleven labeled “It’s complicated.” The categories are AP’s assessments of individual tracked promises, not a single measure of all of Trump’s campaign commitments. The dataset does not state that the overall record was “behind,” identify a target delivery rate, or support a claim about a specific February or March 2026 status. The counts offer a concrete snapshot of the tracker’s distribution as of its recorded last-modified date. Because the retrieved file is not a later archived snapshot, it cannot show how AP changed individual statuses after December 2025. The revised title and account report the published classifications and their scope without inferring a performance trend from the labels.
editorial_notes: Replaces the unsupported general “behind” characterization with the tracker’s exact 25-item status distribution. Date is the dataset’s explicit lastModified value, not the record’s unverified February/March date; no trend is inferred.

proposed_title: AP Tracker Listed Trump’s Birthright-Citizenship Pledge as “It’s Complicated” in Its Dec. 3, 2025 Dataset
description_medium: The AP tracker dataset retrieved October 2, 2026 declares a last-modified date of December 3, 2025. It lists Trump’s promise to end birthright citizenship as “It’s complicated.” That verifies the label in the dated dataset, but it does not establish that the tracker showed the same status on February 28, 2026. AP later reported that the Supreme Court struck down Trump’s order on June 30, 2026, a subsequent legal outcome.
description_long: The Associated Press tracker’s retrieved data lists Donald Trump’s promise to end the constitutional right to birthright citizenship and quotes his pledge to sign an order ending automatic citizenship for children of undocumented immigrants. The row is labeled “It’s complicated.” The AP data file was retrieved October 2, 2026, and its metadata declares a last-modified date of December 3, 2025. This supports the status label as part of that dated dataset, not the title’s claim that the tracker still displayed it on February 28, 2026. AP’s linked coverage explains the legal dispute: Trump signed an executive order seeking to restrict birthright citizenship, and lower courts blocked it. In a later report, AP said the Supreme Court struck down the order on June 30, 2026. That later ruling supplies subsequent context and should not be confused with the earlier tracker snapshot. The updated title anchors the rating to the file’s recorded date, while the description distinguishes AP’s tracker classification from the later judicial outcome. The dataset is not an archived February 28 capture, and no claim is made about status changes after its stated modification date.
editorial_notes: The retrieved AP row directly verifies “It’s complicated,” but its explicit dataset timestamp is Dec. 3, 2025, not Feb. 28, 2026. Corrected title is dated to the evidence. AP’s June 30, 2026 Supreme Court story is later context only.
evidence_notes: Read AP promises.json row: Immigration category; exact promise “End the constitutional right to birthright citizenship”; status “It’s complicated”; AP status_link points to https://apnews.com/article/supreme-court-immigration-trump-birthright-citizenship-83f70d58636219c0ff98c7d765ab2b4d; method_link is the Jan. 20, 2025 White House order. Retrieval metadata gives lastModified Dec. 3, 2025 and retrieval Oct. 2, 2026. Search attempt: system2 query for AP status-link article; generic results initially, then directly opened AP source and found article describing Supreme Court consideration / lower-court blocks. Direct AP open on status-link page succeeded. A separate targeted system2 search for AP June 2026 birthright ruling surfaced AP’s later Supreme Court ruling; used only as subsequent context.

proposed_title: AP Tracker Classified Trump’s Largest-Deportation Promise as “In Progress” in Its Dec. 3, 2025 Dataset
description_medium: The AP tracker’s December 3, 2025 dataset lists Trump’s promise to conduct the largest deportation program in U.S. history as “In progress.” The row quotes his pledge that the “migrant invasion” would end on his first day in office. It does not identify a separate promise specifically about “criminal migrants,” and it does not mark the broad deportation promise “It’s complicated.”
description_long: The AP tracker dataset identifies an Immigration promise: “Conduct the largest deportation program in U.S. history,” accompanied by Trump’s campaign statement that the “migrant invasion” would end on his first day in office. AP labels that row “In progress.” The JSON file retrieved October 2, 2026 declares a last-modified date of December 3, 2025, so the title should present that dated classification rather than claim it was an undated or later status. The row’s promise is the broad mass-deportation pledge; it is not a distinct promise to deport only “criminal migrants.” AP links the row to its campaign coverage of the pledge and to an executive order on immigration enforcement. Its linked March 2026 report describes political debate over the scale and implementation of the deportation agenda, including calls to focus enforcement on people with criminal records and competing pressure to expand removals. That later article provides policy context, not a new tracker status. The revised account corrects the mismatch between the original title and AP’s actual row: the relevant promise was marked “In progress,” not “It’s complicated.”
editorial_notes: Corrects two errors: AP’s promise is the broad “largest deportation program” pledge, not a separate criminal-migrant pledge, and its status is “In progress,” not “It’s complicated.” Dated to the dataset’s stated Dec. 3, 2025 lastModified; later policy reporting is context only.
evidence_notes: Read AP promises.json row: exact promise “Conduct the largest deportation program in U.S. history”; status “In progress”; read-more link is https://apnews.com/article/trump-mass-deportations-latino-voters-ec64f85e3633c9c7a8a247eaf9feb64f; status_link is the AP Immigration hub; method_link is Trump’s Jan. 20, 2025 executive order. Dataset metadata gives 25 promises, lastModified Dec. 3, 2025, retrieved Oct. 2, 2026. Directly opened that AP article and found the headline/body identifying the pledge. Further system2 exact criminal-migrant query did not surface a separate tracker row; the JSON row resolves the status and wording directly.
